pk.context: 10 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

clues.kinetics: Absolute bioavailability is not known, but food does not change exposure. Over 99% is bound to plasma proteins, mainly albumin, and it is metabolized mainly by CYP3A4, with about 50% recovered in urine.
clues.substance: Molecular weight 588.3. A crystalline powder that is insoluble in water and very stable in the solid state.
clues.product: Approved under an NDA as 10 mg film-coated tablets, taken once daily.
clues.safety: Boxed warning for embryo-fetal toxicity. Contraindicated in pregnancy and in hypersensitivity to it; anemia and nasopharyngitis are the most common reactions.
clues.indication: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (WHO Group I) in adults, to reduce the risks of disease progression and hospitalization.
clues.mechanism: Inhibits the binding of endothelin-1 to both ETA and ETB receptors, with high affinity and sustained receptor occupancy.

tell: A boxed warning for embryo-fetal toxicity and an active metabolite with a 48-hour half-life set this PAH endothelin blocker apart.
